answers.reasoning: The introductory page explicitly selects a rotary DC-motor-driven joint with simplifying assumptions; neither every joint type nor retained electrical/flexible states is generally second order.
Actual figure labels shoulder 3, elbow 1 and wrist 3, summing to 7. Hand 4 and neck 3 are separate labels.

The stationary stator provides field, the rotating armature carries winding current, and the commutator switches connection. The parenthetical ironless-winding attribution is not needed for this correct role assignment.
Current connection reverses relative to the rotating winding to keep the developed torque sense consistent for the chosen supply polarity, not to prevent reversal under all voltage polarities.
The right-handed cross product (3,0,0)×(0,4,0)=(0,0,12), multiplied by charge 2, gives (0,0,24) N.
For nonzero B, a parallel or antiparallel velocity makes v×B=0. Perpendicular velocity maximizes magnitude for fixed nonzero speed.
The displayed independent proportional relations give 0.4·3=1.2 N·m and 0.2·10=2 V for the supplied coefficients.
di/dt=(v_A−r_A i_A−k_e ω_m)/L_A. Holding the listed terms fixed except speed, a positive speed rise reduces the derivative.
The actual circuit has an opposing back-EMF source, so L_A di/dt+r_A i=v_A−k_e ω_m.
The numerator is 12−2·1−0.1·20=8 V. Divide by 0.5 H to obtain 16 A/s.
Positive inductance with a bounded voltage difference gives bounded current slope, excluding an instantaneous finite jump without an impulse.
Neglecting the current state is a time-scale approximation: electrical/current regulation must settle much faster than the retained mechanical motion.
For ideal transmitted gear-port quantities, output speed=20/10=2 rad/s and output torque=2·10=20 N·m. Port power is conserved.
Substitute motor speed/acceleration η times the load values into motor torque balance and multiply by η: ητ_m=(I+η²I_m)θ̈+(b+η²b_m)θ̇.
Using motor coordinates instead gives τ_m=(I_m+I/η²)ω̇_m+(b_m+b/η²)ω_m.
The reflected motor inertia is 30²·0.01=9; adding it to 2 and 6 yields 11 and 15 kg·m².
Both interval widths equal 4. The maximum/minimum ratio changes from 6/2=3 to 15/11≈1.364, so relative variation decreases, not absolute variation.
Neglecting I in I+η²I_m requires η²I_m≫I across the operating range, not merely η>1.
A flexible resonance inside the intended bandwidth cannot safely be dismissed as a far-separated unmodeled high-frequency mode.
The explicitly qualified half-resonance heuristic permits ω_n≤30/2=15 rad/s.
Matching coefficients of s²+k_v s+k_p and s²+2ζω_n s+ω_n² yields k_p=ω_n², k_v=2ζω_n.
The largest nominal ω_n is 8/2=4; k_p=4²=16 and critical k_v=2·4=8.
Rotational analogue ω=√(k/I)=√400=20 rad/s; 20/(2π)≈3.18 is hertz, not rad/s.
Half of 20 is 10 rad/s, so k_p=100 and k_v=20 for critical damping.

The source drawing replaces the depicted distributed bending/torsional members by equivalent lumped parameters. Its 0.23 and 0.33 are model-shape approximations, not universal material or gear factors.
m_eff=0.23·4.347=0.99981 kg; √(3600/0.99981)=60.0057 rad/s, dividing by 2π gives 9.5502 Hz. The source’s 9.7 Hz is inconsistent with its own 60 rad/s.
Exact J/B compensation with τ=J(θ̈_d+k_v ė+k_p e)+Bθ̇ gives actual θ̈=θ̈_d+k_v ė+k_p e and homogeneous error dynamics.
Actual θ̈=ρ(θ̈_d+k_v ė+k_p e). Subtracting from θ̈_d yields ë+ρk_v ė+ρk_p e=(1−ρ)θ̈_d.
The opposing physical torque subtracts d/J from actual acceleration, so desired-minus-actual error receives +d/J.
The source’s forward path is controller, motor driver, DC motor, joint/link, measured angle. Encoder feedback returns the angle to the comparator.
A PID box in an architecture diagram does not prove any later code implements PID. The actual p685 code has a constant torque parameter and no error-feedback law.
The source function reads state[0] into theta_dot and returns its angular-acceleration derivative, so it integrates one speed state.
A first-order ODE for speed corresponds to a second-order equation for position; integrating position as a state adds θ̇=ω.
In the printed argument order I_m,b_m,I,b,eta,tau_m, the zeros select load I and b and eta=1 makes motor and load coordinate speeds coincide.
sol.y[0] is the sampled first state, angular speed; np.gradient with sol.t estimates its time derivative numerically.
At steady speed acceleration is zero, giving b_m ω=τ_m and ω=2/0.1=20 rad/s.
The time constant is I_m/b_m=0.1 s, so the zero-initial-speed solution is 20(1−e^(−10t)).
Analytic initial acceleration τ_m/I_m=200 rad/s². The specified forward endpoint difference is 20(1−e^(−0.1))/0.01=190.325..., a lower finite-step estimate.
The plotted speed tends to 20 rad/s and acceleration tends to zero. Torque remains 2 N·m and balances viscous friction.
The excerpt lacks np and solve_ivp imports and t_span, theta_dot_0 and t_eval setup; the motor constants and function body are printed.
The actual code divides the reused speed by eta=10 and multiplies torque by eta: 2 rad/s and 20 N·m. This arithmetic is not a loaded operating-point proof.
At the prior no-load steady speed, b_m ω_m=0.1·20=2 N·m already consumes the commanded electromagnetic torque. The reused no-load speed cannot establish an additional 20 N·m external output.
The ratio sweep solves the ODE anew for each eta with I=1 and b=0.05, extracts load speed, then multiplies by eta for motor speed.
The third list entries pair forestgreen and 20 under zip.
At steady state load speed=ητ_m/(b+η²b_m). Motor speed is η times that, giving η²τ_m/(b+η²b_m).
Motor steady speed=25·2/2.55≈19.6078 rad/s; 10/2.55≈3.9216 is the load speed.
For eta=1 the asymptote is 2/0.15=13.333..., time constant 1.01/0.15≈6.733 s, and speed at 5 s≈6.988. The plot is a finite-time transient, not a contradictory steady value.
Divide motor-speed numerator and denominator by η² to obtain limit τ_m/b_m. Load speed has one fewer factor of η and tends to zero.
Differentiate ητ_m/(I+η²I_m): derivative=τ_m(I−η²I_m)/(I+η²I_m)². It changes positive to negative at η=√(I/I_m)=10, the positive global maximum.
The final expressions use I,I_m,b,b_m,eta_values, not tau_m. A declared constant need not affect every calculation.
NumPy squares the seven entries elementwise and broadcasts the scalar operations; the result remains seven elements.
At 10 reflected inertia is 1 and total is 3; at 20 reflected inertia is 4 and total is 6. The added constant prevents a fourfold increase of the total.
Require η²·0.01>2, or η>√200≈14.142. The first listed ratio above that threshold is 20.
Set 0.05η²=0.2. With positive ratio η=√4=2.
The source explicitly says a current-drive system adjusts v_A to force the desired armature current; inductance still limits current slew.

sourcePageObservations.notes: Title: Lecture 22, Modeling and Control of a Single Joint.
Learning objective only.
Contents roadmap only.
Scoped rotary-joint DC-motor second-order approximation. Figure labels shoulder3/elbow1/wrist3/hand4/neck3; length annotations170,370,340mm are illustrative anatomy, not model parameters.

Stator stationary field; armature rotates carrying current; commutator maintains torque sense. Cutaway labels encoder, commutator, magnet, ironless winding, brush, reduction gearhead, output shaft. The heading Stator (ironless winding) should not silently identify the pictured current-carrying winding as a stator fact. Lorentz qv×B shown.
Torque k_m i_a and back EMF k_e θ̇_m. Signal diagram runs applied voltage to current to torque to motion to speed/back-EMF opposition.
Armature R/L/opposing back-EMF circuit, current differential equation and current-drive adjustment of voltage. Nonzero inductance delays current/torque changes; finite-voltage qualification matters.

Rigid ideal gear η>1, output speed motor/η. Motor balance includes rotor inertia/damping and reflected load torque. Port torque multiplication must distinguish transmitted gear torque from electromagnetic motor torque before rotor/friction losses.

Algebra yields load-coordinate I+η²I_m and b+η²b_m. 2–6 plus9 gives11–15. Relative variation decreases, not absolute span. Motor dominance means reflected contribution, not physical rotor inertia grows.
Finite flexibility in gears, shaft, bearings and link can add modes. Neglect requires sufficiently separated unmodeled resonances; not all physical resonances are automatically high.
Heuristic ω_n≤ω_res/2 where ω_res is lowest structural resonance. High gains can excite unmodeled modes. Normalized polynomial and ω_n=√k_p.
m=b=k=1 partition α1 β=ẋ+x; resonance8→natural4→kp16,kv8. Heuristic does not independently prove arbitrary flexible-system stability.
Equivalent spring–mass or torsional model. k400/inertia1→20rad/s→3.183Hz. Massless shaft means its own distributed inertia neglected, not zero attached inertia.
Lateral cantilever lumping0.23m and rotational0.33I are depicted model-specific factors. 4.347kg×.23≈1kg, stiffness3600→60rad/s. Printed9.7Hz disagrees with60/(2π)≈9.55Hz.

α=I_max+η²I_m and β=(b+η²b_m)θ̇. Printed normalized error dynamics need inertia matching or a ratio qualification, and physical disturbance torque must be normalized. Maximum-resonance gains kp=ω_res²/4,kv=ω_res presume critical normalized design.
PID-controller, driver, DC motor and joint/link diagram with angle encoder feedback. It is architecture, not evidence of PID code implementation.

Actual constant-torque ODE integrates one speed state. args zeros remove load inertia/damping and eta1. Missing imports/time/initial-value/sample setup. np.gradient is finite differentiation, not symbolic exact acceleration.
Speed reaches20rad/s; acceleration decays from near200. Finite endpoint gradient can start lower. Output labels20rad/s≈1145.9deg/s. No position-setpoint convergence shown.

Code reuses prior no-load motor-speed samples and algebraically scales gear speed/torque. Printed20N·m output is not a consistent additional loaded operating point at no-load20rad/s with modeled rotor damping.

Load I1,b.05; ratios1/5/20/50 with steelblue/darkorange/forestgreen/tomato. Each reruns ODE and converts load to motor speed. Legend steady-state asymptotes differ from finite5s endpoint, especially eta1.
New parameters Im.01,bm.05,I2,b.2,tau3; seven-element eta array. Torque declared but unused in effective-parameter arrays. Power operation is elementwise.
All seven table rows independently recalculated: Ieff2.01,2.04,2.25,3,6,11,27 and beff.25,.4,1.45,5.2,20.2,45.2,125.2. Curves quadratic plus constant load baselines.
Recap of reduced joint model, commutator, omitted inductance and squared gear reflection. Same scope qualifications apply.
